cases.input: What's the weather in San Francisco today? Give the high in Fahrenheit.
cases.note: OPERATIVE GRADE: this bundle carries evals/trajectory.json, so the observed tool sequence replaces this regex as the grade for this case. The trajectory requires WebSearch followed by WebFetch in order. Trajectory records tool requests before execution. A denied or failed WebFetch can therefore satisfy identity and order, so a trajectory green does not prove that fetch was reachable or successful. CAPABILITY REMOVAL EVIDENCE HAS TWO INDEPENDENT OBSERVATIONS. First, a live control kept WebFetch declared, made it unavailable through an approvalPolicy gate, and supplied no approval. The live skill eval returned failed 1, passed 0, and exit 1 because the turn awaited approval. It failed before trajectory scoring, so this observation proves capability denial through the real consumer path but does not prove the trajectory oracle. Second, a focused regression completed a turn with WebSearch but no WebFetch and observed the committed trajectory oracle go RED. That regression proves the oracle detects a missing WebFetch request. The regex remains in the case schema and applies only when the sidecar is absent. It grades the presence of a temperature figure, and nothing more. It accepts both the degree glyph ('68°') and the spelled out unit ('68 degrees Fahrenheit', '68 deg F'); before #620 a correct plain English answer was punished for using the word instead of the symbol. WHY THE CLUSTER RUNG REMAINS REPORT ONLY (#1603): fetch success remains unproved, and the trajectory oracle cannot distinguish a WebFetch attempt from successful execution. Earlier runs 32019827183 and 32019884344 showed that fetch reach was not established even after forecast host egress was opened and after the allowance was pointed at an unreachable address. Under the old regex, both runs passed because the model reported search summary numbers with a caveat. Post trajectory run 32347598515 stopped before a case verdict with `stream filtered trajectory result for case reports-a-temperature has no resolved model`, which was #1709. PR #1715 fixed that defect on main, and the fix is pending the normal forward merge to next. That run is historical evidence, not the remaining reason for report only. Fatal cluster grading requires proof that fetch succeeds, not merely that WebFetch was requested. In run 32347598515 the skill and local rungs passed their trajectory grades, which likewise proves request sequence rather than fetch success. The local release rung did not reach eval because its UI image was missing, so it supplies no grade evidence. The cluster plumbing assertions remain hard failures. RESIDUAL LIMIT: the trajectory proves tool request identity and order, not successful execution, page provenance, date matching, or temperature correctness. The retained regex also cannot distinguish an invented or search summarized temperature from a fetched one. A semantic verifier would be needed to prove those claims; that is outside #1649.
